scope.name: Pokemon Card e Base Expansion Pack high-gravity tranche
notes: Japanese Pokemon Card e main expansion released December 1, 2001 with 128 modeled rows in the local catalog.
This pass deepens the release dossier plus nine high-gravity / interface-teaching card rows; the remaining 119 card rows stay generated follow-up work.

context.name_en: Pokemon Card e Base Expansion Pack

sources.title: Local Japanese classic catalog: Pokemon Card e Base Expansion Pack
TCGdex Japanese set endpoint: E1 / Pokemon Card e Base Expansion Pack

claims.text: The local Japanese classic catalog models Pokemon Card e Base Expansion Pack / 基本拡張パック with a December 1, 2001 release date.
The local catalog and TCGdex-derived metadata model 128 card rows for Base Expansion Pack e, with no source-gap rows in the local release file.
Base Expansion Pack e is modeled as a Japanese main expansion in the ポケモンカードe series, using TCGdex set id E1.

Base Expansion Pack e matters because it is not just another checklist: it is Pokemon moving into the e-Card apparatus, where the card frame, numbering, and interface become part of collector identity.

Collector attention naturally gathers around Charizard, the two Mewtwo rows, Pikachu, and the holo Kanto/Johto anchors, but the release-level story is the interface shift into Japanese E1 rather than a pure character ranking.
This source-set pass deepens the release and nine high-gravity card rows only; the other 119 Base Expansion Pack e rows remain generated catalog-history follow-up work.
A Base Expansion Pack e match should preserve Japanese title 基本拡張パック, TCGdex set id E1, local card number, row id, and source-row text together; translated names alone are not enough.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent result says Base Expansion Pack e, Japanese e-Card Base, E1, Expedition Japanese, 基本拡張パック, e-Card Charizard, e-Card Mewtwo, or another high-gravity E1 card.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm Japanese Base Expansion Pack e / E1 identity by title, set id, card number, and row id before treating a card as this release.
steps: Confirm the Japanese release title 基本拡張パック and/or TCGdex set id E1.
Confirm the card number/local id against the local row, especially for famous names that appear in English Expedition or later e-Card products.
Do not treat English Expedition Base Set, later reprints, or same-character cards as equivalent without set/number evidence.
Preserve messy source-row text and normalized collector labels separately when the local source translation is uncertain.
For transactional use, ask for front/back photos, e-Card border/number area, holo features where applicable, and condition-focused surface/corner images.

narrative.human_title: When the card becomes an interface
narrative.why_it_matters: Base Expansion Pack e is an apparatus shift. Pokemon is no longer only arranging monsters on cardboard; it is asking the card to behave like an interface, with a new border language and an E1 spine that agents must preserve. That is why the famous names are almost dangerous here: Charizard and Mewtwo pull attention, but the set identity lives in the e-Card frame, the Japanese title, and the row number.
